messages.content: 你能幫我找到紐約有閱讀室和小說區的公共圖書館，然後在洛杉磯有Wi-Fi和有兒童區的公共圖書館，最後在芝加哥有咖啡廳和閱讀室的公共圖書館嗎？

function.name: public_library_find_nearby
function.description: Locate nearby public libraries based on specific criteria like English fiction availability and Wi-Fi. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city and state, e.g. Boston, MA

facilities.description: Facilities and sections in public library.

message.reasoning:
The user wants to find public libraries in three cities with certain facilities. They want:

1. In New York (NY), libraries with Reading Room and Fiction section.
2. In Los Angeles (LA), libraries with Wi-Fi and Children Section.
3. In Chicago, libraries with Cafe and Reading Room.

We need to call the function public_library_find_nearby for each location with appropriate facilities. The function expects a single argument object with location string and facilities which can be one of the enumerated strings: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe". But the facilities field seems to accept only one value? It says "Facilities and sections in public library." The type is union of those strings. That suggests we can only pass one facility at a time. But we need multiple facilities per query. The function signature might not support multiple values. However, maybe we can pass an array? The type says "facilities: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[]". Wait, the type shows "facilities: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[],", but the syntax is ambiguous. It might mean facilities can be either a string or an array of strings. The type annotation shows "facilities: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[],", which could be interpreted as facilities can be one of those strings or an array of those strings. So we can pass an array of strings. Let's do that.

Thus we will call the function three times:

First: location: "New York, NY", facilities: ["Reading Room", "Fiction"].

Second: location: "Los Angeles, CA", facilities: ["Wi-Fi", "Children Section"].

Third: location: "Chicago, IL", facilities: ["Cafe", "Reading Room"].

We need to output the results. We'll call the function for each.
